summary.one_liner: FastAgency is an open-source framework for taking multi-agent workflows written with the AG2 (formerly AutoGen) framework from prototype to production, exposing them as a console app, web chat app, or REST API.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a common programming interface so a workflow written once can run under a console UI (ConsoleUI) or a web UI (MesopUI). Workflows can be served through a FastAPI REST adapter (FastAPIAdapter) or a NATS.io message broker adapter (NatsAdapter) for distributed setups. It can import an OpenAPI specification and connect it to agents as an external API integration. It includes a Tester class intended for continuous integration pipelines and a command-line interface for running workflows. A Cookiecutter template generates a project with a default workflow, devcontainer, Docker scripts, and Fly.io deployment scripts with GitHub Actions.
use_cases: turn an AutoGen/AG2 notebook prototype into a web app
serve multi-agent workflows over a REST API
run agent workflows distributed across machines via a message broker
connect an OpenAPI spec (e.g. weather API) to LLM agents
test multi-agent workflows in CI pipelines
deploy agent workflows to Fly.io or Docker
notable: Write a workflow once and reuse it across ConsoleUI and MesopUI
Chainable network adapters: FastAPI for REST, NATS.io for scalable distributed deployment
One-line-style integration of OpenAPI specifications into agents
Cookiecutter template generates project, devcontainer, and deployment scripts
Currently AG2 is the only supported runtime
caveats: Only AG2 (formerly AutoGen) is supported as a runtime at present; other frameworks are planned
Deployment to Fly.io requires a Fly.io account and API token; LLM use requires an OpenAI API key (the template defaults to OpenAI)
Windows local serving uses waitress instead of gunicorn
